text: That evening: Holmes says the bed must always stay in the same position to the ventilator and the rope
why: Holmes says at ¶216 that the bed must always stay in the same position relative to the ventilator and rope, and the scene is set at dusk at the Crown Inn.

text: Why was the bed in the middle room clamped to the floor? — to keep the bed always in the same position to the ventilator and the rope
id: q.why_bed_clamped=to keep the bed always in the same position to the ventilator and the rope
why: The bed is clamped (¶214) and Holmes gives the same reason at ¶216. The explanation is Holmes's inference, but it is a possibility the story gives reason to consider.

text: What, if anything, came through the ventilator into that room? — it has to arrive at one spot: the bed is kept always in the same position to the ventilator and the rope
why: The question is plainly open ('if anything'), and the whistle, the ventilator, and the fixed bed give reason to consider something arriving at a fixed spot. The story never confirms what came through.

text: What was the bell-rope put there for? — the bed is clamped so as to stay always in the same position to the rope and the ventilator
why: The dummy rope is fixed above the ventilator (¶151), and Holmes says the bed cannot move (¶216). Tying the bed's position to the rope is a possibility the story has raised.

text: What was the bell-rope put there for? — it was clearly never meant for a bell-pull
why: Holmes says at ¶216 that the rope 'was clearly never meant for a bell-pull', and ¶149–151 establish it is a dummy not attached to any wire.

text: What was the ventilator really put there for? — the bed is clamped so as to stay always in the same position to the ventilator
why: Holmes calls the ventilator 'ventilators which do not ventilate' (¶157) and says the bed is fixed relative to it (¶216). The purpose given is a reasonable possibility, though it is only Holmes's theory.

text: Why would Helen have to be moved into the middle room in particular? — the bed cannot be moved from its place by the ventilator and the rope, so the sleeper has to be brought to it
why: Helen was moved to the middle room (¶67), and Holmes suspects the move was an excuse (¶136). With the bed fixed relative to the ventilator and rope (¶216), the idea that the sleeper must be brought to it is a possibility the story gives reason to consider, though not confirmed.

text: Why was the bed in the middle room clamped to the floor? — the lady could not move her bed, which must stay in the same position to the ventilator and the rope
why: Holmes says at ¶216: 'The lady could not move her bed. It must always be in the same relative position to the ventilator and to the rope.'
